questions.q: What does the RPM filter require?
options: A barometer and a GPS module
questions.explain: Bidirectional DShot and an ESC that supports it: the filter needs the RPM over the return channel.

options: The lower bound of the notch
questions.explain: If the bound is above the motor's real frequency, the filter sits off target from the noise.

questions.q: Why should the minimum bound on a 10" drone be lower than on a 5"?
questions.explain: Frequency = RPM/60. Big props — slow motors — low frequency.

questions.q: In the viking10 case rpm_filter_min_hz was 100, while the median motor frequency was 91 Hz. The consequence?
options: The filter didn't see the motors
questions.explain: For most of the flight the RPM filter sat above the motor frequency: 80–150 Hz noise was barely filtered, D-term +44.5 dB.

questions.q: What does the DSHOT_TELEM flag (before 4.5 — RPMFILTER) in the OSD on arming mean?
questions.explain: At least one ESC isn't reporting telemetry — arming is blocked.

questions.q: After save, bidir is OFF again. What is this?
options: The firmware rolled the setting back
A broken ESC or its firmware
questions.explain: After every save, read the values back with get.

questions.q: rpm_filter_q = 500 sets the notch width to roughly:
questions.explain: Q is in hundredths; 500 → Q factor of 5.

questions.q: What attenuation of the motor peaks after the RPM filter is normal?
The RPM filter is enabled, but the spectrum in Blackbox didn't change. What in this diff explains the problem?
questions.fragment:
# diff
set motor_pwm_protocol = DSHOT600
set dshot_bidir = OFF
set rpm_filter_harmonics = 3
set rpm_filter_min_hz = 100
options: dshot_bidir = OFF: without bidirectional DShot there's no eRPM, so the notches have nothing to tune to
rpm_filter_harmonics = 3 is excessive: the third harmonic eats phase and masks the result
rpm_filter_min_hz = 100 cuts off all the notches: this 5"'s motors spin below 100 Hz in hover
DSHOT600 is too fast for telemetry: the RPM filter works only on DSHOT300
questions.explain: The RPM filter takes motor frequencies from eRPM telemetry; without dshot_bidir there is none, and no notches are placed.
